title: Design a Basic Elevator
description: Model elevator state, direction, stops, and door operations.

data.text: Design a single elevator for a 10-floor building. It must handle internal requests (buttons inside) and external requests (buttons on each floor), respect direction, and not exceed capacity.
Elevator is the main class. It holds current floor, direction, capacity, and a sorted set of requested floors. Door and Request are value objects.

data.title: Elevator and Request
Why SortedSet?
data.text: SortedSet automatically keeps floors in order. For up stops, ascending order works. For down stops, we use a descending comparer so the elevator visits the highest floor first when going down.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Separate up and down stops to respect direction
SortedSet gives O(log n) insertion and nearest-floor lookup
Direction changes only when current queue is empty
data.takeaway: A simple elevator needs two sorted queues and a direction state. The real complexity appears when multiple elevators share requests.
